elimination.reason: A faction at 0 influence eliminates only its owner; while another opponent is left the game goes on, so the two-player assertion that the game ends (a winner, a draw, no further actions) or that nothing else changes does not hold.

turn-cycle.reason: The turn order runs through the bystanders' seats: state.turn counts every seat's turn, and text that fires at the start or end of each turn or of an opponent's turn (and a delayed effect or a skipped Restore Rule counted in turns) also fires on a bystander's turn.

bystander-responses.reason: Every player in the game other than the controller may respond to an action, so a response window lists, offers, logs or ends with the bystander too (an endTurn is answered by every other player; the priority holder once all have passed is the last seat).

silenced-opponent.reason: "Your opponent cannot respond" silences the one opponent selected for that text; the other players in the game may still respond, so a window opens for them.

player-count.reason: The answer depends on how many players there are: the seat list, the players of a save, the candidates of a pick of "an opponent" or of a player's faction (no longer forced), the factions that can be attacked.

seat-swap.reason: Emergency Obfuscation's seat swap applies for a card a fixture put straight into play once the harness has selected its opponent (at two seats it never starts applying), and it changes who controls the card and whose turn it ends.
